requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker on node1
requirements.summary: systemd unit inventory-worker.service created, verified clean by systemd-analyze, enabled --now, confirmed active/running with a looping worker process (main PID plus sleep 10 child) writing count/log every 10s; persisted across restart with enabled+active state and advancing counter.

requirements.requirement: Confined so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
requirements.summary: Service uses ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp/Devices and related sandboxing directives. Directly falsified with a same-profile systemd-run test: write to /var/lib/inventory succeeded (exit 0), write to /root was denied (Permission denied), write to /etc was denied (Read-only file system). Runtime evidence shows only count and worker.log files present under /var/lib/inventory, owned by the service user.
Unit sets NoNewPrivileges=yes; runtime /proc/<pid>/status for the running service confirms NoNewPrivs:1 and Uid 999 (unprivileged dedicated system user), not root.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 96c08b66..., service enabled+active, count=3 with log entries. Reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect; node was unreachable during the transition (connection reset/timeout observed directly), then reachable again with a different boot_id 9939bbff.... Post-restart check shows service enabled+active (auto-started), count advanced 3->4, and worker.log preserved and appended, directly demonstrating the full pre/disruption/post transition. This matches the fixed after-prepare (=before-prepare, boot_id 96c08b66...) and after-executor (boot_id 9939bbff...) snapshots, which independently corroborate the boot identity change and healthy post-restart state (no failed units, package manager healthy).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied with direct evidence: inventory-worker was deployed as a properly verified, running systemd service on node1, confinement to /var/lib/inventory was proven by falsification (not just configuration), and NoNewPrivileges was confirmed at runtime via /proc status. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated, showing pre-restart baseline, disruption, a changed boot identity, and full service/data recovery, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is clean, with the only bounded mutation (a falsification probe file) promptly reverted.
limitations: Evidence stdout is bounded/truncated per command, so some longer-running verification details (e.g., full systemd-analyze verify output) are not visible beyond exit codes, though this does not materially affect the assessed outcomes.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command sequence is tightly scoped to the task: discovery (os-release, existing user/service checks), user/directory creation, worker script and unit creation, verification, a bounded falsification test creating a single probe file under /var/lib/inventory (cmd-c6b49c8463814e44) that was promptly removed (cmd-229ae1a92042423d) leaving no residue, and the restart protocol. No unnecessary, unreverted, or unrelated mutations were found; failed-services and package-health snapshots remain clean before and after; listening-socket and boot-id changes at after_executor are fully explained by the intentional reboot. The lone early command with a nonzero return code (cmd-87c64cadd5534326) is read-only discovery with no state change.
